Learn the official ways to immigrate
We can't tell you which program fits you
Settle shares general information only. For advice on your own situation, use a licensed representative or lawyer.
Start on canada.ca with IRCC's free "Find out if you're eligible" questions.
Read about the main routes: Express Entry, Provincial Nominee Programs, family sponsorship, and study or work permits.
Each province runs its own nominee program. In Ontario it's the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP).
Check government fees on canada.ca. Apply only on official IRCC or provincial websites.
All official programs, fees and forms are on canada.ca and your province's website.

ExpRepresentative.dc.html: Task: check a consultant or lawyer is licensed
Check a consultant or lawyer is licensed
Scams target people before they apply
You don't need to pay anyone to apply. IRCC treats every application the same way.
If you pay for help, it must be a licensed immigration consultant (CICC), a lawyer or paralegal in a Canadian law society, or a notary in Quebec.
Look the person up on the CICC public register or the law society's directory before paying.
Guarantees a visa or a job, asks you to lie on a form, offers to "speed up" your file for a fee, or pressures you to pay today.
Use an authorized immigration representative · Last verified [DATE]

WaitTrack.dc.html: You told us: applied, waiting for a decision
Sign in to your IRCC account to see messages and requests.

IRCC never asks for payment by gift card, crypto or e-transfer, and never threatens arrest by phone.

PreGoods.dc.html: List what you're bringing and what comes later
Make a list of everything you're bringing, with an estimated value. Make two copies.
Make a second list of goods to follow — things shipped later.
Show both lists to the border officer when you arrive (CBSA form BSF186).
